subtopicTitle: Cross product — formula, direction (right-hand rule), torque/area calculation

cards.front: What is the scalar magnitude formula for the cross product of two vectors, $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$?
cards.back: The magnitude of the cross product is given by: $$||\vec{A} \times \vec{B}|| = ||\vec{A}|| \cdot ||\vec{B}|| \cdot \sin(\theta)$$ where $\theta$ is the angle between vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ ($0 \le \theta \le \pi$).

cards.front: How do you determine the direction of the cross product vector $\vec{C} = \vec{A} \times \vec{B}$?
cards.back: The direction is determined by the **Right-Hand Rule**: Point the fingers of your right hand in the direction of the first vector ($\vec{A}$), then curl them towards the second vector ($\vec{B}$) through the smaller angle. Your thumb will point in the direction of the resulting cross product vector ($\vec{C}$). This direction is perpendicular to the plane containing both $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$.

cards.front: What is the geometric interpretation of the magnitude of the cross product, $||\vec{A} \times \vec{B}||$?
cards.back: The magnitude $||\vec{A} \times \vec{B}||$ represents the area of the parallelogram formed by placing vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ tail-to-tail.

cards.front: How is torque ($\vec{\tau}$) defined using the cross product of the position vector ($\vec{r}$) and force vector ($\vec{F}$)?
cards.back: Torque is defined as: $$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$$ The magnitude is $||\vec{\tau}|| = ||\vec{r}|| \cdot ||\vec{F}|| \cdot \sin(\theta)$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{F}$. The direction of the torque vector is perpendicular to the plane containing $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{F}$, determined by the right-hand rule.

cards.front: Given $\vec{A} = A_x\hat{i} + A_y\hat{j} + A_z\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = B_x\hat{i} + B_y\hat{j} + B_z\hat{k}$, write $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$ in determinant form and expand it.
cards.back: Determinant form: $$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ A_x & A_y & A_z \\ B_x & B_y & B_z \end{vmatrix}$$ Expanded form: $$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = (A_yB_z - A_zB_y)\hat{i} - (A_xB_z - A_zB_x)\hat{j} + (A_xB_y - A_yB_x)\hat{k}$$

cards.front: What is the cross product of two parallel vectors, $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$, and why?
cards.back: The cross product of two parallel vectors is the zero vector: $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{0}$. This is because the angle $\theta$ between parallel vectors is either $0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$. Since $\sin(0^\circ) = 0$ and $\sin(180^\circ) = 0$, the magnitude $||\vec{A} \times \vec{B}|| = ||\vec{A}|| \cdot ||\vec{B}|| \cdot \sin(\theta)$ becomes zero.

cards.front: Is the cross product commutative? If not, how does $\vec{B} \times \vec{A}$ relate to $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$?
cards.back: No, the cross product is not commutative. It is **anti-commutative**. This means that reversing the order of the vectors reverses the direction of the resulting vector: $$\vec{B} \times \vec{A} = -(\vec{A} \times \vec{B})$$ The magnitude remains the same, but the direction is opposite, as dictated by the right-hand rule.
